page: Microsoft Azure ND128isr_GB300_v6 is a specialized, hardware-isolated GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for high-performance computing, large-scale deep learning, and advanced AI workloads. Running on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features an arm64 processor architecture providing 128 dedicated vCPUs alongside 864 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 6.75 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware acceleration is provided by four NVIDIA Blackwell GB300 GPUs, delivering an aggregate 1,152 GB of GPU memory. For high-speed local scratch space and high-throughput data ingestion, the server integrates 16,459 GB of NVMe SSD storage. In addition, the instance is RDMA capable and supports Azure Premium Storage, facilitating low-latency inter-node communication and scalable external persistent storage.

The hardware configuration is characterized by high resource density across accelerator memory and local solid-state capacity rather than general-purpose computing. With 1,152 GB of total VRAM and over 16 TB of local NVMe SSD capacity, the instance is built for large language model training, massive model inference, and data-intensive scientific computing tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure ND128isr_GB300_v6 is an isolated GPU-accelerated instance engineered for demanding artificial intelligence and high-performance computing workloads. Powered by an arm64 CPU architecture, the system provides 128 dedicated vCPUs, 864 GB of system RAM (6.75 GB per core), and four NVIDIA Blackwell GB300 GPUs delivering 1,152 GB of total GPU memory. Storage infrastructure includes 16,459 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD space alongside support for Premium Storage. The instance is built on Microsoft Hyper-V and incorporates RDMA networking capabilities to enable low-latency node-to-node interconnects in distributed clusters. With substantial accelerator memory and high-capacity local storage, the hardware profile eliminates common I/O bottlenecks in data-heavy training pipelines. This server type is targeted at large language model training, multi-GPU AI inference, complex scientific simulations, and high-throughput parallel data processing pipelines.
